broken.what: S1 'traps it so it can't move around' is correct (mucus traps pathogens), but it was labelled wrong and T1 replies 'But trapping them isn't enough' without confirming it.
T3 gives the answer (the acid kills most pathogens) and then asks 'What do you think that acid environment does to the pathogens?'. The question was already answered.
T4 offers to finish explaining stomach acid. The student says 'k', but T5 drops stomach acid and jumps to white blood cells.
T7 asks for the WBC vs RBC difference, which T5 had just stated. T8 then asks for the 'fancy scientific name', which T7 had just given (leucocytes). The student only has to parrot it.

T9 offers to explain the two types and the student says yes. T10 instead repeats the nucleus fact and asks 'What do we call this type of white blood cell?' without saying which type. The question cannot be answered.
T15 asks what the lymphocyte produces before lymphocytes have been introduced at all.
T20 asks what the long-lived lymphocytes are called, and T21's question contains the answer: 'What do we call those special memory cells?'

S24 'you dont get sick cos its gone quick' is correct but gets no acknowledgement. The tutor asks 'Shall I just tell you the rest?', the student says 'nah im good', and T25 explains anyway, ignoring the no.
T25/T26 re-ask what happens to the pathogen, which the student already answered correctly in S24.
Markdown bold is shown as raw asterisks: **non-specific**, **antigen**, **antibody**, **antitoxin**.
T28 says 'You've got a really solid understanding' to a student who said 'im lost' and got most answers told to them.

would_quit.why: The student has complained 'too long' four times. The tutor keeps asking questions about things it never taught (T10, T15), or re-asking what it just said, so the student feels lost and is being quizzed for nothing.

fixes.change: Render **bold** markdown as <strong> instead of showing raw asterisks.

Explicitly confirm a correct student answer before moving on (S1, S24). Never ask a question whose answer appeared in the same or the previous tutor turn (T3, T8, T21, T25). Never ask about a term or cell type before it has been introduced (T10, T15).
If the student says yes to 'shall I explain X', explain X in the very next turn (T5 and T10 failed this). If they say no, skip the explanation and move on (T25 failed this).

fixes.target: tutor brevity rule for bored learners
fixes.change: After a 'too long'/'skip' signal, keep each turn to 2 short sentences plus one question. Make the closing praise match how the student actually performed.

Keep the app title on one line with ellipsis or hide it under 420px, and stop it being clipped. Give the breadcrumb chip max-width with ellipsis. Add top spacing so '← Home' is not overlapped by the page heading on 02-subjects-phone.
